cls: Long-acting beta-2 adrenergic agonist (LABA) - inhaled bronchodilator
pharm: Stimulates beta-2 adrenergic receptors on airway smooth muscle, producing rapid and sustained (about 12-hour) bronchodilation; used twice daily for maintenance of COPD
quick: One 20 mcg/2 mL nebuliser vial twice daily (morning and evening); max 40 mcg/day
Limited data; use only if benefit outweighs risk
Unknown if excreted in milk; use with caution
No specific guidance; use with caution
Lung function (FEV1), heart rate, blood pressure, potassium, glucose
summary: Formoterol is a long-acting beta-2 adrenergic agonist (LABA) indicated for the long-term, twice-daily maintenance treatment of bronchoconstriction in adults with COPD (chronic bronchitis and emphysema). The nebuliser solution dose is one 20 mcg/2 mL unit-dose vial inhaled twice daily (morning and evening), with a maximum total daily dose of 40 mcg. It is not indicated for acute deteriorations of COPD and is not a rescue inhaler; short-acting beta-agonists are used for acute relief. Formoterol is not indicated to treat asthma, and LABA monotherapy (without an inhaled corticosteroid) is contraindicated in asthma because of an increased risk of serious asthma-related events including death. Common effects include tremor, palpitations, headache and, with excessive use, clinically significant cardiovascular effects, hypokalaemia and hyperglycaemia.
indications: Long-term, twice-daily maintenance treatment of bronchoconstriction in adults with COPD, including chronic bronchitis and emphysema
(Inhalation powder/aerosol formulations are also used in combination with an inhaled corticosteroid for asthma maintenance; not for acute relief)

dosage.d: One 20 mcg/2 mL vial twice daily (morning and evening); do not exceed 40 mcg/day
dosage.t: Inhaled via standard jet nebuliser with air compressor
dosage.n: Not for acute deterioration; partly used vials discarded

dosage.d: Per the specific ICS/LABA combination product label (e.g. 4.5-12 mcg twice daily as inhalation powder)
dosage.t: Inhaled, twice daily, always with an ICS
dosage.n: LABA monotherapy is contraindicated in asthma

admin: For oral inhalation only - never for injection or oral ingestion
Nebulise the unit-dose vial via a standard jet nebuliser connected to an air compressor (e.g. PARI-LC Plus with PRONEB Ultra)
Store nebuliser vials in the foil pouch and remove only immediately before use; discard partly used vials
Do not use to relieve acute symptoms; keep a short-acting beta-agonist for rescue
Do not exceed the prescribed dose or combine with other LABA-containing products
If the usual maintenance response fails, seek medical advice promptly as this may signal destabilisation of COPD
moa: Formoterol is a selective long-acting beta-2 adrenergic agonist. By binding beta-2 receptors on bronchial smooth muscle it activates adenylyl cyclase, raising intracellular cyclic AMP, which relaxes airway smooth muscle and produces bronchodilation. Its lipophilicity gives a depot effect at the receptor, conferring a long (about 12-hour) duration of action while retaining a relatively rapid onset. At higher than recommended doses beta-2 stimulation also causes skeletal-muscle tremor, tachycardia, hypokalaemia and hyperglycaemia.

absolute: Use of a LABA, including formoterol, without an inhaled corticosteroid in patients with asthma
Known hypersensitivity to formoterol or any excipient
monitor: Heart rate, blood pressure and ECG/QT in at-risk patients

preg: There are limited data on formoterol use in pregnancy. Beta-agonists may interfere with uterine contractility, and animal data show effects at high doses. Use during pregnancy only if the expected benefit to the mother justifies the potential risk to the fetus; poorly controlled COPD/asthma itself poses risks.
lact: It is not known whether formoterol is excreted in human milk, though it is found in the milk of lactating animals. Caution should be exercised when administered to a breastfeeding woman; weigh the benefit of breastfeeding against the mother's need for the drug.
renal: No specific dose adjustment is recommended in renal impairment; formoterol is extensively metabolised and pharmacokinetics in renal impairment have not been specifically characterised.
hepatic: Formoterol undergoes hepatic metabolism (glucuronidation and O-demethylation); specific dosing guidance in hepatic impairment is not provided, so use with caution and monitor.

major: Other long-acting beta-2 agonists - do not co-administer; additive cardiovascular toxicity that may be fatal
Drugs that prolong the QT interval (Class IA/III antiarrhythmics, some antipsychotics, MAO inhibitors, tricyclic antidepressants) - increased risk of ventricular arrhythmias
moderate: Non-potassium-sparing diuretics - additive hypokalaemia and ECG changes
Beta-blockers - antagonise bronchodilation and may cause severe bronchospasm; use cardioselective agents cautiously if essential
interactions.diagnostics: May lower serum potassium and raise blood glucose; can affect ECG (QT interval, T-wave changes)

serious: Clinically significant cardiovascular effects (tachyarrhythmias, marked blood-pressure change) with excessive use
Serious asthma-related events if used as monotherapy in asthma
emergency: Paradoxical bronchospasm with acute breathlessness - discontinue immediately

monitoring: Heart rate and blood pressure, especially with cardiovascular disease
Serum potassium in patients at risk of hypokalaemia
ECG/QT interval in patients on QT-prolonging therapy
counsel: This is a maintenance inhaler taken twice a day - it is NOT a rescue inhaler; keep your blue/short-acting reliever for sudden symptoms
If you have asthma, only use formoterol together with a steroid inhaler as prescribed - never alone
Do not take more than the prescribed dose or use two long-acting inhalers together
Tell your doctor if your usual reliever is needed more often or your breathing worsens
Possible shakiness, fast heartbeat or headache usually settle; report chest pain or sudden worsening of breathing
Use nebuliser vials straight from the foil pouch and discard any leftover solution
pk: Bronchodilation within about 1-3 minutes of inhalation
Bronchodilator effect persists about 12 hours (twice-daily dosing)
Store nebuliser vials refrigerated/at room temperature per label, in the foil pouch, away from heat and light; protect from freezing
pearls: Maintenance bronchodilator, NOT a reliever - patients must keep a short-acting beta-agonist for acute symptoms
LABA monotherapy is contraindicated in asthma (risk of asthma-related death); asthma use requires concomitant inhaled corticosteroid
Rapid onset (~1-3 min) yet ~12-hour duration distinguishes it from salmeterol
Do not exceed 40 mcg/day or combine with another LABA - excess causes serious, potentially fatal cardiovascular effects
Watch for hypokalaemia and hyperglycaemia, especially with diuretics, steroids or in diabetics
missed: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember unless it is nearly time for the next dose; in that case skip the missed dose and continue your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one.
overdose: Overdose causes exaggerated beta-agonist effects: tremor, headache, marked tachycardia or arrhythmia, palpitations, hypertension or hypotension, hypokalaemia and hyperglycaemia, and potentially fatal cardiac events. Treatment is supportive with cardiac monitoring; a cardioselective beta-blocker may be considered with caution (risk of bronchospasm), and serum potassium should be monitored and corrected.
